title: One more question
setting: Late at night at the family home. Kenji has an English speaking test tomorrow, and he comes to his big sister Yuki, who uses English at work, with a question.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: neechan, chotto ii? shitsumon ga aru n da kedo.
lines.ja: ねえちゃん、ちょっといい？質問があるんだけど。
lines.kana: ねえちゃん、ちょっといい？しつもんがあるんだけど。
lines.english: Sis, got a sec? I've got a question.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: neechan tte, eigo hanaseru yo ne?
lines.ja: ねえちゃんって、英語話せるよね？
lines.kana: ねえちゃんって、えいごはなせるよね？

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: eigo? hanaseru yo. shigoto de mo hanashiteru shi. nande?
lines.ja: 英語？話せるよ。仕事でも話してるし。なんで？
lines.kana: えいご？はなせるよ。しごとでもはなしてるし。なんで？
lines.english: English? Sure I can. I speak it at work, too. Why?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: ashita, eigo de shitsumon ni kotaeru tesuto ga aru n da.
lines.ja: 明日、英語で質問に答えるテストがあるんだ。
lines.kana: あした、えいごでしつもんにこたえるてすとがあるんだ。
lines.english: Tomorrow I've got a test where you have to answer questions in English.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: boku, eigo hanasenai kara, shitsumon ni kotaerarenai yo.
lines.ja: 僕、英語話せないから、質問に答えられないよ。
lines.kana: ぼく、えいごはなせないから、しつもんにこたえられないよ。
lines.english: I can't speak English, so there's no way I can answer the questions.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: daijoubu. mijikai kotae de ii n da yo. demo, kotaenai no wa dame.
lines.ja: 大丈夫。短い答えでいいんだよ。でも、答えないのはダメ。
lines.kana: だいじょうぶ。みじかいこたえでいいんだよ。でも、こたえないのはだめ。
lines.english: It's fine. Short answers are okay. But not answering at all is a no-no.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: sore, benkyou ni naru. neechan, atama ii ne.
lines.ja: それ、勉強になる。ねえちゃん、頭いいね。
lines.kana: それ、べんきょうになる。ねえちゃん、あたまいいね。
lines.english: That's really useful. You're smart, Sis.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.ja: ありがとう。じゃあ、何か質問ある？
lines.kana: ありがとう。じゃあ、なにかしつもんある？

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: uun, nai. metcha benkyou ni natta. jaa, oyasumi.
lines.ja: ううん、ない。めっちゃ勉強になった。じゃあ、おやすみ。
lines.kana: ううん、ない。めっちゃべんきょうになった。じゃあ、おやすみ。
lines.english: Nope. I learned loads. Okay, night.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, chotto! benkyou wa? tesuto, ashita da yo ne?
lines.ja: え、ちょっと！勉強は？テスト、明日だよね？
lines.kana: え、ちょっと！べんきょうは？てすと、あしただよね？
lines.english: Hey, hold on! What about studying? Your test is tomorrow, right?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: shita yo. datte ima, benkyou ni natta mon.
lines.ja: したよ。だって今、勉強になったもん。
lines.kana: したよ。だっていま、べんきょうになったもん。
lines.english: I did study. I just learned loads, didn't I?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sore wa benkyou shita tte iwanai no!
lines.ja: それは勉強したって言わないの！
lines.kana: それはべんきょうしたっていわないの！

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: a, neechan. mou hitotsu shitsumon ga aru n da kedo.
lines.ja: あ、ねえちゃん。もう一つ質問があるんだけど。
lines.kana: あ、ねえちゃん。もうひとつしつもんがあるんだけど。
lines.english: Oh, Sis. I've got one more question.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.ja: ううん。お腹へった。何かある？
lines.kana: ううん。おなかへった。なにかある？
lines.english: Nope. I'm starving. Is there anything to eat?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.ja: その質問には答えません！
lines.kana: そのしつもんにはこたえません！
lines.english: That is not a question I will be answering!

choices.english: Yuki practises English questions with Kenji, and he stays up late studying for his test.
Yuki gives Kenji a tip for his speaking test; he calls that studying, says goodnight, then asks for food.
Kenji explains to Yuki how to answer questions in English at work, and she thanks him for it.

questions.explanation: Line 5: Kenji has a test tomorrow where he has to answer questions in English, and in line 7 he says he can't speak English, so he won't be able to answer them. Line 8: Yuki's tip: short answers are fine, but not answering is a no-no. Line 11: he says he learned loads (metcha benkyou ni natta) and says goodnight. Lines 12-14: when Yuki asks about studying, he claims that learning from her tip counts (ima benkyou ni natta mon), and she tells him it doesn't (sore wa benkyou shita tte iwanai no). Lines 15-18: his 'one more question' is that he's hungry, and she refuses to answer it. A is wrong: nobody practises any English, and Kenji heads off to bed (line 11: jaa, oyasumi) without studying. C swaps the two of them: Yuki is the one who speaks English at work (line 4), the test is Kenji's (line 5), and the tip comes from Yuki (line 8).

questions.english: At the end of a meeting, Tanaka-san asks the room, "dewa, nanika shitsumon wa arimasu ka?" (Well then, are there any questions?) You have one. Say so.
questions.ja: では、何か質問はありますか？
questions.kana: では、なにかしつもんはありますか？
questions.romaji: dewa, nanika shitsumon wa arimasu ka?
questions.answer: Say you have a question with shitsumon ga aru, in polite form for Tanaka-san: hai, hitotsu shitsumon ga arimasu.

modelAnswers.ja: はい、一つ質問があります。

modelAnswers.romaji: a, sumimasen. shitsumon ga aru n desu kedo.
modelAnswers.ja: あ、すみません。質問があるんですけど。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, excuse me. I have a question.

questions.explanation: A question you have is aru: shitsumon ga arimasu, or shitsumon ga aru n desu kedo to lead into it. English 'have' points to motsu, but shitsumon o motte imasu is not how it's said. Kenji opens with the casual version in line 1 (shitsumon ga aru n da kedo) and again in line 15 (mou hitotsu shitsumon ga aru n da kedo). Yuki's nanika shitsumon aru? in line 10 is the casual version of Tanaka-san's question, with ga dropped after nanika. Once you've said it, go on and ask: asking is shitsumon suru, or just kiku.

questions.english: Kenji tells Yuki why he's worried about tomorrow's test. What did he say?
questions.ja: ケンジくんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじくんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji-kun wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: I won't be able to answer the questions (with o, as in English 'answer the questions').
I won't be able to ask any questions.
I won't be able to answer the questions.

questions.explanation: Line 7: boku, eigo hanasenai kara, shitsumon ni kotaerarenai yo. In Japanese you answer to a question, so shitsumon takes ni: shitsumon ni kotaeru, here in the can't-form kotaerarenai. Line 5 has the same ni (eigo de shitsumon ni kotaeru tesuto), and so does Yuki's last line (sono shitsumon ni wa kotaemasen). A is English 'answer the questions' put into Japanese word for word, with o: with kotaeru, o marks what you give as the answer (namae o kotaeru, give your name), never the question. B, shitsumon dekinai, means he can't ask questions. In the test the teacher asks, and Kenji's worry is answering.

questions.english: At work, Mai covers the phone with her hand and whispers, "ne, eigo dekiru? eigo no denwa na n da kedo." (Hey, can you do English? This call's in English.) You can speak a little. Tell her.
questions.ja: ね、英語できる？英語の電話なんだけど。
questions.kana: ね、えいごできる？えいごのでんわなんだけど。
questions.romaji: ne, eigo dekiru? eigo no denwa na n da kedo.
questions.answer: Say you can speak a little, with hanasu in its can-form: un, chotto dake hanaseru yo.

modelAnswers.ja: うん、ちょっとだけ話せるよ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I can speak a little.

modelAnswers.ja: 英語？少しなら話せるけど。
modelAnswers.english: English? I can speak a bit, I guess.

questions.explanation: Being able to speak a language is the can-form of hanasu: hanaseru (polite hanasemasu). Kenji asks it that way in line 3 (eigo hanaseru yo ne?), Yuki answers hanaseru yo in line 4, and Kenji's hanasenai in line 7 is the negative. Plain hanasu says you do speak it, like Yuki's shigoto de mo hanashiteru (I speak it at work, line 4), not that you can. Mai's eigo dekiru? asks the same thing as eigo hanaseru?, so answering with hanaseru fits. eigo de hanasu would be talking in English right now.

questions.english: Yuki asks about studying, and Kenji answers, "shita yo. datte ima, benkyou ni natta mon." Has he actually studied for the test?
questions.ja: ケンジくんは、勉強しましたか？
questions.kana: けんじくんは、べんきょうしましたか？

choices.english: No. Yuki's tip taught him something, but he hasn't sat down and studied.
Yes. He studied on his own earlier that evening, before he asked Yuki.
Yes. He practised answering English questions with Yuki.

questions.explanation: benkyou ni natta means something was instructive: he learned from it. It's the thanks phrase he uses for Yuki's tip in line 9 (sore, benkyou ni naru) and line 11 (metcha benkyou ni natta). benkyou shita means he sat down and studied, and in line 13 Kenji passes one off as the other. Yuki's line 14, sore wa benkyou shita tte iwanai no, says exactly that: that isn't called studying. B is wrong: his only reason is what he learned just now (ima), and nobody mentions him studying earlier. C is wrong: Yuki only gave him a tip; they never practise, and he says goodnight right after (line 11).

newWords.english: big sister (what a younger brother or sister calls her; casual)
something, anything (nanika aru? = is there anything?)
say, call; X tte iwanai = that isn't called X
